- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or neutral, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean reversion bias.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) — cap forecast rise to 2–4% after spike, then allow gradual decay.
- Forecast mean reversion is weak — if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model should not predict further decline; instead, expect slight rebound.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses early correction after sharp drops — adjust downward by 1–2% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 0.67), model tends to overcorrect — dampen forecast volatility by 10–20% in such cycles.
